## Ticket

`docs/tickets/489e_P37.61e__byte-budgets-to-warnings.md` — manifest row
489e (Round 11 / P37, sub-round 11D), under operator **RULING E-4**
(GATE DECISIONS 2026-11-15; `docs/build/readouts/RULINGS-2026-11-15.md`):
*"Byte budgets become warnings, not failures … keep the shape checks
hard … one generous hard ceiling: the CURRENT STATE block plus the
ledger head stay ≤ 18 KiB."* Live verification explicitly disabled —
no live legs, no production mutation, `main` untouched.

## What this changes

- **Every byte budget is advisory (ADR-252).** In
  `docs/build/tools/ledger_contract.py`: `orient-budget` (>12 KiB —
  the >8 KiB level was already a warning), `cs-budget` (>3 KiB),
  `returnPass-line-budget` (>1,024 B — new rule, split out of
  `line-budget`), `entry-budget` (>2 KiB — now warns in the current
  PHASE LOG region too, matching the older regions) and `probe-budget`
  (>48 KiB) emit `warning`, never `error`. In the vendored
  `scripts/docs/check-build-memory.sh`: each `guarded ledger-budget`
  byte cap is `warn ledger-budget` under new tagged SIG-LOCAL hunks
  (L9, L14, and L8's byte half); **L5 retires** — the >48 KiB orient
  probe returns to upstream 0.5.0's own `warn` byte-for-byte, so the
  hunk is gone, not weakened.

- **Every shape check stays hard.** CURRENT STATE key order and
  declared vocabulary, keys outside the block (`key-shadow`),
  `| PRIOR` history, the returnPass comma-id-list grammar, the
  ≤256 B per-line CURRENT STATE rule, the PHASE-LOG append target and
  the `## OPEN FINDINGS` boundary remain `rep.v`/`guarded`. In the
  script the bundled `guarded ledger-budget` id is split **before**
  any demotion (RULING E-4's explicit requirement): new still-guarded
  `ledger-shape` carries the ≤256 B CS lines, `| PRIOR`, the
  returnPass grammar, the key-shadow rule and the append target;
  `ledger-budget` keeps only byte budgets. Same split in
  `ledger_contract.py`: `line-budget` stays hard for every key's
  ≤256 B line; new `returnPass-line-budget` warns over the L8-raised
  1,024 B.

- **One new additive hard ceiling.** `head-ceiling`
  (`ledger_contract.py`) / `ledger-ceiling` (vendored script,
  SIG-LOCAL L15): the CURRENT STATE block plus the ledger head
  (orient region) read ≤ **18,432 B** combined — replacing the
  separate 12 KiB + 3 KiB hard fails with one bound sized to a single
  ~20 KB agent read. `guarded`/`rep.v`: it fails.

- **The "notes-file budget" is named unmatched.** Phase-4
  enumeration found no dedicated check id for it; the 2 KiB
  PHASE-LOG entry budget is the bound the recorded "slide line"
  repairs actually served. Nearest generic flag — the `size` check's
  >1 MB-fixture / >5 MB-file warnings — already warns. Nothing
  silently dropped; recorded in ADR-252 decision 5.

- **`memory_guard.py` verified consistent — unchanged.** It carries
  no byte budgets (sha256/prefix byte-identity append-only machinery).

- **Vendored provenance.** The banner now declares eighteen tagged
  hunks (L1–L4, L6–L16 live + L5 recorded retired; three P34.x-era
  hunks — `* _TEMPLATE.md` readout glob, the P34.28 grandfather
  retirement, the §8b living-lint block — predate the L-numbering and
  were tagged `SIG-LOCAL` in place under this PR so the claim is
  literally true). The verification recipe now diffs the **pinned**
  upstream (release 0.5.0, commit `8aeb6dc`, sha256 `f48a365d…`):
  the installed `~/.claude/skills` copy has drifted to a newer
  upstream and shows that drift too. Audited group-by-group: 23 diff
  groups = 18 logical hunks, all tagged.

- **Never fold unless archived** — unchanged: the only escape stays
  the verbatim-archive convention under
  `docs/build/reports/memory-repair/`; the ADR records it (decision 6).

## G10 self-amendment — the retired-violations list

This PR changes checks that judge it. Under G10 the unchanged base
checks were re-run on this tree. **No committed record trips a
shape rule and the live ledger is inside every old byte bound**
(head 1,767 B ≪ 12 KiB; CURRENT STATE 1,299 B ≪ 3 KiB; no
current-region PHASE LOG entry over 2 KiB; orient recipe ≪ 48 KiB),
so the base checks pass on the final tree outright — the PR retires
**severity classes**, not live violations. The classes retired
(would-have-been violations, now warnings):

- `ledger_contract.py`: `orient-budget` >12 KiB · `cs-budget` >3 KiB ·
  `entry-budget` >2 KiB (current region) · `probe-budget` >48 KiB ·
  `line-budget` on the `returnPass` line >1,024 B (the shared-cap
  bundle — the ≤256 B other-key half stays hard, it is not retired).
- `check-build-memory.sh`: `guarded ledger-budget` on the orient
  >12 KiB cap, the CURRENT STATE >3 KiB cap, the `returnPass` >1,024 B
  cap (shared-$cap bundle — ≤256 B half moved to `ledger-shape`,
  not retired), current-region PHASE LOG >2 KiB, and SIG-LOCAL L5's
  >48 KiB probe guard.
- New hard checks added (violations they *create*, none fired on this
  tree): `head-ceiling` / `ledger-ceiling` >18 KiB combined.
